unit.cmd: python -m pytest tests/ -q && python tools/gate/gate.py selftest && python tools/review/panel.py selftest && python tools/audit/append_only.py selftest && python tools/audit/append_only.py check && python tools/audit/routing_accuracy.py selftest && python tools/audit/routing_accuracy.py report && cd intent-control-plane && uv run pytest -q
unit._note: every automated-test entrypoint in the repo, including both oracles' own selftests
unit._timeout_note: Raised 300 -> 900 on 2026-07-31 with the measurement rather than by feel. The 300s budget was set when the root suite was 70 tests in about 47s. It is now 331 tests in 182s, and this domain chains FOUR commands: the root suite, the gate selftest, the panel selftest, and the intent-control-plane suite at about 50s. Total is roughly 250s on an idle machine and it timed out at 300s three times on 2026-07-31 under concurrent load, which produced a FAIL that named no failing test and sent two diagnoses down the wrong path. The honest alternative is splitting this into unit and subproject domains so a slow subproject cannot mask a fast regression; that is a contract shape change and is deferred to a ticket rather than done inside a timeout bump. Falsifier: if the suite passes 600s this number is hiding growth again and the split is overdue.
unit._ext_note: Added 2026-08-19, closing an EXT-1/EXT-3 gap a fresh audit found on main: both tools/audit/append_only.py (EXT-1, append-only ledger enforcement) and tools/audit/routing_accuracy.py (EXT-3, router-vs-spawn agreement) existed with green selftests since 2026-08-17 (TODO.md EXT section, both checked [x]) but were invoked by nothing in this contract or in ship-gate.yml -- a real oracle reporting into a terminal nobody gated on, the exact shape the `skills`/`pointers`/`rules` domain notes above already name as a recurring defect in this repo. append_only.py's `check` subcommand is a real pass/fail oracle (exit 1 on a truncating writer) and now blocks this domain on FAIL. routing_accuracy.py has no pass/fail threshold by design (it is a measured number, not yet a gate criterion; TODO.md's own row records 17% agreement as the finding, not a violation) so only its `report` runs here for visibility and its `selftest` is what actually gates (proving the counter can detect a planted mismatch). Both add well under 1s to this domain, measured 2026-08-19.

The unit domain's own _timeout_note, written 2026-07-31 and so six days after this reason, sets a 900s budget with an explicit falsifier at 600s. Separately, intent-control-plane/repo_health.py enforces FILE_BUDGET, FUNC_BUDGET and CLASS_BUDGET, a maintainability budget rather than a perf one, and it is referenced by no pyproject script, by gate.py, or by CI, so it runs nowhere. The Lighthouse and p95-without-a-threshold halves of the original claim were re-checked by grep and still hold. N/A is retained because a duration budget on the gate's own run is not what this domain measures, but the enabling half landed today: gate runs now record duration_seconds and domain_seconds, so the unit falsifier is evaluable for the first time. The 8571 rows before that carry no duration at all. Whether that becomes a real perf domain is a contract shape decision and belongs to the operator, with the evidence in docs/analysis/2026-08-08-na-domains-rechecked.md.

docmap._note: Every tracked markdown file has a derivable or declared lifecycle status, and docs/DOCMAP.md matches what the documents imply. Declared 2026-07-31, six days after the tool was written: docmap ran clean the whole time and NOTHING enforced it, which is the same shape as a hook that cannot fire. A hand edit to DOCMAP.md reads as drift and fails, exactly as CODEBASE-MAP.md does, because both are generated. The residue that cannot be derived lives in docs/doc-status.txt, currently 44 rows against a stated ceiling of 37; growth past that means the derivation rules are wrong rather than that the registry should grow.

dashboard._note: Added 2026-08-19, closing a gap a fresh audit found on main: 39 dashboard/ source files merged across DASH-1 slices 1-3 (5a61a91..ca055da) with 0 test files invoked by anything in this contract or in ship-gate.yml, invisible to CI the same way EXT-1/EXT-3 were. dashboard/core has real Rust unit tests (16, ledger readers + meme parsing + module toggles, all tolerant-of-malformed-input per the program-design spec) and dashboard/src-tauri is a real Tauri 2 crate; `cargo test --workspace` runs both from one command since they share dashboard/Cargo.lock as a workspace. Measured 2026-08-19 on this machine (which is also the ship-gate.yml self-hosted runner's host, same HOME): `cargo check --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` both exit 0 with GTK3 + webkit2gtk-4.1 present (pkg-config confirms both), src-tauri compiles clean, dashboard/core's 16 tests pass in under a second. This is an extra domain per gate.py's own 'DOMAINS is the floor, not the ceiling' rule (tools/gate/gate.py:1116), the same mechanism `rules`/`skills`/`pointers`/`docmap` already use, so no gate.py code change was needed to make it required and blocking.
dashboard.scope_note: This domain is Rust-only on purpose: `dashboard/web`'s `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build) was ALSO measured green here 2026-08-19 (Node 22 via nvm, 1830 modules, built in ~4s) but is deliberately not folded into this cmd, because ship-gate.yml's `gate` job installs Python only (actions/setup-python@v5) and has no Node toolchain step; adding an npm command to this domain's cmd would make it FAIL on every CI run until that step is added, which is a workflow change, not a contract change. See ship-gate.yml's dashboard-web-build step, added alongside this domain in the same change, which runs the npm build directly as a CI step rather than through gate.py. If GTK3/webkit2gtk-4.1 are ever missing on a runner (they were not, here), the honest fix is scoping this cmd to `cd dashboard/core && cargo test` and stating that narrowing here, not silently dropping src-tauri from `--workspace`.

lint._note: Stack-lint oracle, phase 1: C4/PERF/PIE + import sorting, configured in ruff.toml. Enforces the coding-style standard from intent-control-plane's pyproject.toml on the root tools/ tree. Action #2 from 2026-08-13 code-quality-rethink. Phase 2 adds SIM/B/ERA; phase 3 adds UP/E/F/D after batch fixes.

spec._note: non-trivial source changes (>3 files) require a docs/specs/ entry touched in the same change. Spec culture already exists (20 specs on disk); this is the enforcement half. Action #4 from 2026-08-13 code-quality-rethink.

blast_radius._note: Computes the transitive Python import blast radius of changed files. Informational: always passes, reports which modules are affected and flags wide-radius changes (>=3 importers). PRD #16.

lane_enforcement._note: The most recent state/claims.jsonl row must name lane A (claude-setup harness). Cross-lane work is the most frequently logged lesson; this domain makes the gate fail before the session produces work under the wrong charter. Filed 2026-07-29, implemented 2026-08-30.

todo_inbox._note: TODO.md's generated prompt-inbox block must match the intent store. Exits N/A when the store is absent (CI runners), FAIL when the block is stale. Enforces the intent lifecycle: a captured prompt is visible in the todolist until triaged, and a todolist that passed against a store it could not read would hide every prompt in the estate.

refute._note: Every claim in state/claims.json has a falsifier, and none of them fire. The refutation engine runs each claim's own verification command; any REFUTED or BROKEN verdict fails the gate. Claims whose preconditions are not met on the runner (e.g. no deployed ~/.claude) report cannot-measure and do not count toward the exit code.

bus_integrity._note: The hash-chained event bus ledger (state/bus.jsonl) is intact. Every chained row's hash covers its own content plus the previous hash, so any edit, deletion, or reordering of chained rows is detectable. Pre-chain rows (before chaining was added) carry no hash and are reported but not failed.

skilleval._note: Every skill with a routing fixture routes correctly (the right skill wins the prompt). Skills without fixtures are counted as uncovered but do not fail. A skill whose fixture routes to the wrong skill fails the gate. Catches regressions in skill descriptions that would misroute prompts.

prose_fit._note: prose_metrics.py collects density and variance scores to state/prose-scores.jsonl but explicitly defers thresholds (L-2026-07-31-b). This domain verifies that percentile bands have been fitted from the corpus (state/prose-thresholds.json exists, was fitted from 20+ scores, and has not gone stale as the corpus grew). The actual per-document enforcement is a follow-up in slop_lint.py; this domain ensures the infrastructure exists.

skip_tracker._note: L-2026-07-29-i: a generator bug deleted content from 12 shipped files, four tests responded with pytest.skip() instead of failing, the suite reported '89 passed, 4 skipped', and the gate read that as PASS. This domain parses pytest summary lines for each test suite, compares skip counts against state/skip-baseline.json, and fails when skips rise above the baseline. A rising skip count is the signal the gate was missing. Run `update` to reset the baseline after legitimate skip changes.

branch_health._note: Stale branches (merged into the default branch but not deleted) and orphaned worktrees are the two shapes of git debris that have caused gate failures in this repo. The codemap domain excludes .claude/worktrees from compileall because a sibling worktree carried live conflict markers. This domain catches the debris before it causes a downstream failure.

lesson_check._note: state/lessons.jsonl is an append-only ledger of operational lessons. This domain validates that the ledger is parseable and structurally sound: every row has an id, IDs use a recognised format (L-YYYY-MM-DD-x or legacy L###), and the file contains valid JSON. Schema completeness gaps in older rows are reported as warnings rather than failures because the ledger is append-only and pre-existing gaps cannot be retroactively fixed.

coverage_map._note: Added 2026-08-19, operator-approved extension prompted by an external review (Agentica) that independently converged on the same DASH-1 finding as this session's own audit, and named the general fix: the gate should fail CLOSED on undeclared module coverage, not silently pass. Every domain above (build/unit/types/.../dashboard) answers 'does ITS OWN command exit zero'; none of them answers 'is there a top-level directory in this repository that NO domain looks at at all'. dashboard/ was exactly that for two days before a manual audit found it. This domain closes the general case: docs/coverage-map.txt must carry a row (covered-by:<domain> or exempt) for every top-level TRACKED directory (git ls-files, top segment only), and a directory with no row FAILS the gate rather than passing by default -- the inverse of docs/prior-art/out-of-scope.txt's own stated default ('a prefix not listed here is IN scope'), inverted on purpose because unlisted-and-silently-fine is the exact failure mode this domain exists to close. tools/audit/coverage_map.py's first real run against this repository found the check is not merely theoretical: nexus-engine-rs (a second Rust crate, 8 #[test] functions, its own README documenting `cargo test`) has the identical shape dashboard/ had and is recorded in docs/coverage-map.txt as an ADMITTED exemption naming the gap, not a silent pass -- wiring it is a follow-up, out of scope for this change.
